clue.text: Honour kept us doing our share, at first

indicators.note: at first tells us to take only the opening letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Someone praised for keeping a group pulling its weight from the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' takes the initial letter of each word in 'kept us doing our share'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kudos is praise and prestige earned for an achievement, a near synonym of honour.

clue.text: Chessman — frequently he has move sideways in game

parts.note: the king is the most important chess piece
oft is an old word for often
castling in chess moves the king two squares sideways along its back rank, with a rook

explanation.surface: A chess commentary: a piece that keeps stepping sideways during play.
explanation.walkthrough: Every piece of the surface sits in chess, so 'game' looks like part of the chess picture; it is the definition, a children's game of holding a mound against all comers.
explanation.definitionFit: The title names a children's playground contest in which one player holds a mound against the others.

clue.text: Met socially by arrangement — how old-fashioned!

definitions.meaning: went out on a date with someone
out of date, no longer current

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs that arranging a social meeting is terribly behind the times.
explanation.definitionFit: To date someone is to meet them romantically by appointment; something dated has gone out of style.

clue.text: Money needed — bob Cratchit lacks it

parts.note: a bob was a shilling in old British money, abbreviated s

indicators.note: lacks tells us to drop the letters of the word it from the name before

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dickens's poor clerk Bob Cratchit is short of the cash he needs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like Cratchit's first name, but it is the old shilling (S). 'lacks it' removes IT from CRATCHIT, leaving CRATCH. Bob Cratchit is the underpaid clerk in Dickens's A Christmas Carol.
explanation.definitionFit: Scratch is slang for money, cash in hand.

clue.text: Refuse to deal with man reported for crime

parts.note: to black goods or a firm is to boycott them, as in a union action

indicators.note: reported means the word for man is heard rather than seen, giving a different spelling

parts.note: a man is a male

explanation.surface: A man is turned away after being accused of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'black' something, a British trade-union term, is to boycott it.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortion by threat of exposure is a serious criminal offence.

clue.text: Dance round

explanation.surface: Two words: a dance, and something round.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is both a formal dancing party and a spherical object.

clue.text: Pit — home to chap from Ethiopia?

parts.note: an abyss is a deep pit
in means at home
Ian is a man's name, a typical chap

explanation.surface: A deep pit serves as the dwelling of a man from East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia; the question mark admits the definition is a dated one.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the former name of Ethiopia, so its native is described that way.

clue.text: Flier erks let loose

indicators.note: let loose tells us the letters are freed to rearrange themselves

parts.note: erks are RAF ground crew in slang

explanation.surface: Junior RAF ground crew release a bird into the air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let' looks like part of the indicator 'let loose' but it is also fodder: ERKS LET rearranges to the bird. An 'erk' is British slang for a lowly aircraftman.
explanation.definitionFit: A kestrel is a small falcon, a bird of prey that flies and hovers.

clue.text: 18 RN devastated in American cemetery

indicators.note: devastated means wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: a reference to the answer to clue 18 down
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Royal Navy man, wrecked by grief, at a war grave in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'devastated' rearranges ANTILOG (the answer to 18 down) together with RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Arlington National Cemetery in Virginia is the best-known US military burial ground.

clue.text: Abandon the pitch after grass fissure appears

indicators.note: after puts the words the pitch behind the grass and fissure pieces

parts.note: a lea is grassland, a meadow
a vein is a crack in rock filled with mineral
taken as written
to pitch and to lurch both mean to roll or lunge suddenly

explanation.surface: Players walk off a sports field when a crack opens in the turf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pitch' reads as a sports field but means a sudden roll or lurch, as of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to desert someone at a moment of difficulty.

clue.text: National universal gathering, as you might expect

parts.note: Nat. is an abbreviation of national
U is the film-classification abbreviation for universal
a rally is a mass gathering

explanation.surface: A nationwide meeting of all comers is no surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally is an adverb meaning of course, unsurprisingly.

clue.text: Saucy way of dancing?

parts.note: the name of a spicy Mexican sauce is also the name of a Latin dance style

explanation.definitionFit: The same Spanish word names both a tomato-based relish and a lively Latin American dance.

clue.text: Working as an exciseman?

definitions.meaning: an exciseman collects duty, the tax on goods, so whimsically he is dealing with duty

explanation.surface: Asks whether a customs officer is working.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means at work; and since excise is a tax, a tax collector is jokingly concerned with that sort of levy.

clue.text: Divorce unfortunately gets near

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things gone awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A divorce sadly brings a separated couple closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfortunately' rearranges GETS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to separate or alienate, as divorce separates a couple.

clue.text: Working together, against the stream

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
a current is a flowing stream of water

explanation.surface: Swimmers cooperate to battle upriver.
explanation.definitionFit: Concurrent describes things running at the same time or acting in cooperation.

clue.text: Landing a score, with a chance for more?

definitions.text: a score, with a chance for more?
definitions.meaning: in American football this six-point score is followed by a conversion attempt for extra points

explanation.surface: An airline pilot or a football coach talking about results.
explanation.definitionFit: An aircraft's arrival on the ground and a scoring play in American and rugby football share the name.

clue.text: Where espaliers run wild

definitions.meaning: espaliers are fruit trees trained flat against a supporting wall or trellis

explanation.surface: Fruit trees trained on a frame spread unchecked.
explanation.definitionFit: Trained fruit trees grow against garden brickwork; and the idiom means driven crazy.

clue.text: Permitted to board in the French fashion

parts.note: le is a French word for the
ton is fashionable style or society, as in bon ton

explanation.surface: Allowed onto a ship in the Gallic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the French fashion' reads as one phrase but splits: the French word for 'the' plus TON, an old word for high fashion.
explanation.definitionFit: Passengers allowed onto a bus or train are admitted aboard.

clue.text: Run in the next race

indicators.note: in shows the letters sit inside the words next race

explanation.surface: Entering the following heat of a competition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' looks like a verb about racing; in cricket a run not scored off the bat is a bye or wide, collectively called extras.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bye or wide is a run not credited to the batsman, recorded separately.

clue.text: Number of calculations, not quite a contradiction in terms

indicators.note: not quite tells us to drop the final letter of the word for a contradiction

parts.note: antilogy is a contradiction within a statement

explanation.surface: Sums that don't quite contradict themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: An antilog (antilogarithm) is the number whose logarithm is given, used in calculations; 'not quite' cuts the final Y from ANTILOGY.
explanation.definitionFit: An antilogarithm is the number obtained by reversing a logarithm, a figure used when calculating.

clue.text: Rally heading for island noticed a bird

parts.note: to rally someone is to tease them, to chaff them; heading for just places this piece in front of the island
inch is a Scottish word for a small island

explanation.surface: A rally heading for an island sees a bird on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rally' looks like a gathering or a motor race but is an old verb meaning tease. An INCH is a small Scottish island, as in Inchcolm.
explanation.definitionFit: The chaffinch is a common European finch with a pink breast.

clue.text: It's a lot of money, given the price of music

parts.note: for means in exchange for, as in sold for five pounds
a tune is a piece of music

explanation.surface: Getting a large sum for a song.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'for a song', meaning very cheaply: here a mere tune earns the opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortune is a very large sum of money.

clue.text: Erupt violently, trapped in field without a gap

indicators.note: trapped in shows one piece is enclosed by the other
without signals that the letter a is removed from the field word

parts.note: an area is a field of activity
taken as written

indicators.note: violently means the letters are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: Lava bursts out, caught in a field with no outlet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' twice over here: it removes the A from the field word, while 'trapped in' sets the rearranged eruption (from 'violently') inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperture is an opening or hole.

clue.text: While making speech, express resentment of wedding

indicators.note: making speech means we hear the word spoken, so its spelling can change

parts.note: to bridle is to bristle with indignation

explanation.surface: A guest grumbles during the speeches at a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making speech' signals a sound-alike: BRIDLE, to bristle with resentment, sounds like the adjective of the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Bridal is the adjective for things belonging to a bride or her marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Falling over too much, I had the same again

indicators.note: falling over turns the joined words for excessive and I had upside down in this vertical light

parts.note: OTT is short for over the top, excessive
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone drank to excess and toppled, and did it again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falling over' turns the combined OTTID upwards. Ditto marks indicate repetition of the item above.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto means the aforementioned again, a repetition of what was just said.

clue.text: I study an item on the menu

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A diner examines a dish listed on the bill of fare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'menu' suggests a restaurant, but this is a computer menu, where small pictures stand for programs.
explanation.definitionFit: On a computer screen a small clickable picture represents a program or command.

clue.text: Follow right dog around

indicators.note: around shows the word for dog wraps itself about the abbreviation for right

parts.note: to dog someone is to tail them

explanation.surface: A hound circles the right way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dog' looks like a noun but is the verb to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To trail someone is to track or pursue them.

clue.text: Come upon variant spelling of 'nocturne' without an e

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the rearranged letters surround the e
a variant spelling suggests the letters of the quoted word are rearranged

parts.note: the letter e as written

explanation.surface: A pedant notes another way to write the night piece, minus one vowel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but it means outside: the rearranged NOCTURNE goes around an E rather than dropping one.
explanation.definitionFit: To encounter is to meet by chance.

clue.text: Give instruction in English, varying in length

indicators.note: varying means altering, so the letters of the following words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teaching English with lessons of different durations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'varying' rearranges IN LENGTH to NLIGHTEN, after E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: To enlighten is to educate, to give someone knowledge.

clue.text: See husband manage to retire in time

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw backwards, so the joined words for husband and manage are read in reverse

parts.note: to cope is to manage

explanation.surface: Seeing that a husband manages to retire early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is only a linking word, inviting the solver to look; 'to retire' turns the whole of HCOPE round.
explanation.definitionFit: An epoch is a long period of history, an era.
